names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 12 iulie, «Sfântul Cuvios Mihail Maleinul», with the rank word left off.

Read out of saint.gr's line for 12 Ιουλίου, «Όσιος Μιχαήλ ο Μαλείνος πνευματικός πατέρας του Αγίου Αθανασίου του Αθωνίτη», with the rank word, the surname and the description left off. The page gives his name in the world as Μανουήλ.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 12. јул ст. ст., „Преп. Михаил Малеин.“ — „Преп.“ is the rank, which `types` already carries, and „Малеин“ is a **by-name and not a see**: it is the mountain he withdrew to turned into a surname, and §6 keeps a by-name, so the form is the two words the heading leaves. `foldchk.py` returns no holder and `sr-foldpred.mjs` predicts a new key with no other holder — and **the by-name is what keeps it so**, a bare «Михаил» folding with every Michael this corpus has, which is the second time in three days that §6 has kept a form out of a very deep fold.

saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 12ης Ιουλίου — «Όσιος Μιχαήλ ο Μαλείνος πνευματικός πατέρας του Αγίου Αθανασίου του Αθωνίτη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 12 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the surname is the folder's own: the Romanian line reads «Sfântul Cuvios Mihail Maleinul» and the Greek «Όσιος Μιχαήλ ο Μαλείνος». He is the corpus's only Maleinos. The Greek page gives the family and the reigns the Romanian did not, but no year of birth or death, so no `dates` object is proposed: it places him from the reign of Constantine VII to the years of Basil II the Bulgar-slayer, which is a stretch of about eighty years and not a bracket for his life. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence, and the page prints no hymn under his line.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 25.07.2026 (12. јул ст. ст.) — „Преп. Михаил Малеин.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, with its closing full stop, which is what §4 asks for and what `srbody.mjs` now hands back. The identification is the by-name and the mountain and the disciple: „Михаил Малеин“ is this folder’s own name, „повуче се на гору Малеа, код Св. Горе“ is the Mount Maleon the by-name comes from, „од којих је најзнаменитији св. Атанасије Атонски“ names the disciple this folder already relates in both directions, and the Romanian and Greek rows stand on this very 12 July. **`dates` WRITTEN WHERE THE FOLDER HAD NONE, AND THE BOOK’S OWN HEDGE IS KEPT IN THE DISPLAY.** The folder held `dates: null`. This book ends „Скончао мирно око 940 год.“ — he ended peacefully about 940 — so `death` is 940 to 940, basis traditional, display **«about 940»**, the qualifier being the book’s own word and the same treatment «end of the 4th century» had on 9 July: **the hedge is kept in the display and is not turned into numbers**, because any boundary invented for «about» would be invented. This is not the „вероватно“ of 5 July, which was a probability and was refused outright; «око» is a precision and not a doubt. It is also not a narrowing — there was no interval to narrow. `types` UNTOUCHED at `venerable` and `abbot`: „Преп.“ is the `venerable`, and the `abbot` the folder already holds is not in this heading and is not taken away by its silence. **`wonderworker` is not on offer** and nothing in the body offers it. No `office`. No `locations`: Mount Maleon and the Holy Mountain are a narrative. No new `related` rows. **WHAT IS NEW IS THE RENUNCIATION AND THE MEANS.** He was of noble and rich birth, and „Презревши земна блага у младости“ — having despised earthly goods in his youth — withdrew to Mount Maleon, where he struggled „чистећи своје срце постом и молитвом“, cleansing his heart with fasting and prayer; and he had many disciples afterwards, of whom the most notable was Athanasius. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Întru tine, părinte, cu osârdie s-a mântuit cel după chip; că luând crucea ai urmat lui Hristos; şi lucrând ai învăţat să nu se uite la trup, că este trecător; ci să poarte grijă de suflet, de lucrul cel nemuritor. Pentru aceasta şi cu îngerii împreună se bucură, Preacuvioase Părinte Mihail, duhul tău.

source.text: doxologia.ro, «Troparul Sfântului Cuvios Mihail Maleinul», Glasul 8 — the common troparion of a venerable father, printed here with his name

english.text: In you, father, what was made after the image was saved with diligence; for taking up the cross you followed Christ, and by your labour you taught us to look past the flesh, which passes away, and to care for the soul, which is a thing immortal. Therefore your spirit rejoices together with the angels, most venerable father Michael.

death.note: The folder held no dates at all; neither doxologia nor saint.gr gave a year. The Охридски пролог for 12. јул ст. ст. ends „Скончао мирно око 940 год.“ The qualifier «око», about, is the book’s own and is kept in the display rather than turned into a wider interval, any boundary for it being invented.
